findings.summary: The steward's output schema still says the brief is required for every proposal above the limit. This contradicts the new prompt, and the plan leaves it unchanged and does not list it as a dependent.
findings.evidence: outputs.rs:320 reads `/// The owner's brief. Required for a proposal above your limit; null for any other item.` on `pub brief: Option<StewardBriefOutput>`. outputs.rs:325 describes the brief as the fields 'that let the owner decide a proposal'. JsonSchema turns these doc comments into schema descriptions, and the model reads them: outputs.rs:691 says 'The reader sees the rule as the field's description in its schema', and the test at :702 reads schema[...]['description']. The grep for 'above your limit' finds only this line and the old STEWARD_PROMPT line (roles.rs:124), which the plan rewrites. The new routing sends any briefed change to the owner at any rung. A model that follows the schema will brief every over-limit proposal, so the owner gets non-env/token decisions again. That defeats the request's measure: how few decisions reach the owner. Fix: Add crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs to Files and Dependents. Reword the doc comment on StewardItemOutput.brief to say: only when the fix needs an environment change or a token or credential Athena lacks, with the owner's action in if_yes; null otherwise. Make the matching change to the StewardBriefOutput doc. Add an outputs.rs test that reads schema['$defs'/...]['brief']['description'] (in the style of the urgent_reason test at :702) and asserts the new wording and the absence of 'above your limit'. Say in the docs that this description, like the prompt, is prose-only.
findings.location: Decision 7 ('the schema is unchanged') and Dependents; crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs:320 and :325

findings.summary: Once needs_owner is brief.is_some(), the page never renders a card without a brief, so the 'No brief written yet' path in Brief::new can no longer be reached from the page.
findings.evidence: render() at xtask/src/decisions.rs:370-376 calls Brief::new only when needs_owner is true. The plan keeps Brief::new unchanged and keeps a_proposal_without_a_brief_shows_its_title_and_says_none_is_written, testing it only through Brief html directly. Fix: Either remove the no-brief branch from Brief::new and its test, or state in the module docs that it is kept only as a fallback for direct callers. Do not leave a page path documented that cannot happen.

findings.summary: A briefed repeated-failure item is recorded with kind Proposal and loses its RepeatedFailure kind.
findings.evidence: In decide() at steward.rs:717, kind is copied from change.kind. The plan overrides it to Proposal whenever a brief is present, so status and records no longer show the item as a repeated failure. Fix: State this in roles-and-ladder.md and D169: a briefed item of any kind is recorded as a proposal so that the owner surfaces, which filter on kind Proposal, can find it.

summary: I checked the plan against the code by reading it. It is sound. Routing by whether a brief is present matches the accepted reading, and the three places it changes are the right ones: decide() at steward.rs:693-726, open_proposals and in_limit at work_decisions.rs:43-68, and needs_owner at xtask/src/decisions.rs:94. The round-1 blocker is fixed: WorkItem::validate at records/work.rs:131 needs evidence on any item that is not a blind spot, and blind_spot_needing_owner supplies it. The dependents of open_proposals, split_open and in_limit match what grep finds: status.rs:541, drain.rs:4227 and 4320, the drain.rs seeded_proposals fixture (used at lines 5416, 5764, 6297 and 6361), the cli work_decisions.rs fixture, and audience.rs. Each demonstration names a real seam (Counting applier, steward_scenario, run_steward, the xtask page_with helper). One major gap remains, and the plan says it does not exist ("the schema is unchanged"). The steward's output schema still tells the model the brief is "Required for a proposal above your limit". The model reads schema field descriptions (outputs.rs:691-702 shows this design). So code-supplied text would still tell the steward to brief every over-limit proposal, and each briefed proposal now goes to the owner. That works against the request's goal of fewer owner decisions. The fix is small: change two doc comments and add one test.
